output.methodChoice: EDF v0.3 applied internally. I collected two items: X9 (van-level join of service, pads, route days, drivers) and then X1 (Northfield job cards, stores log, warranty paperwork).
output.brief:
Mariana, the cause is very probably water-contaminated brake fluid from one garage, not driver technique, the new pads or the reporting app. All 11 vans with soft-pedal complaints were serviced at Northfield during the bay closure. Eleven of Northfield's 13 vans complained; none of the 25 vans serviced elsewhere did, though every van ran Upper Wend on 9–16 days and the same drivers reported nothing in other vans. Northfield's records show those 11 got fluid from a bulk drum open since March with a missing cap; the two vans given new-drum fluid haven't complained. Two retested vans had fluid boiling at about 150°C versus 255°C for sealed stock; complaints stopped once it was renewed, pads untouched. Upper Wend exposed the fault; it didn't create it. Northfield's 25 Sep warning email went unanswered.

This week: pull the Northfield-serviced vans, test and renew their fluid from sealed stock, and answer Northfield. Don't issue warnings; they'd silence reporting and punish the wrong people. Hold off on retraining and a pad-supplier change; the squeal data are muddied. I'm about 90% sure of the cause; complaint counts after renewal will confirm it.
